Selection barriers

Why an extensive service list is not proof of delivery capability

A controls integrator, hardware supplier and industrial maintenance contractor offer different expertise. The buyer needs verifiable evidence that fits the plant.

01

Unspecified integration claims

PLC models, network protocols, SCADA versions and device interfaces constrain compatibility. No supplier can be assumed to connect every machine without a site review.

02

Downtime claims ignore migration conditions

Planned outages, testing, fallback controls and acceptance depend on the installation. A promise of zero downtime requires project-specific engineering proof.

03

Maintenance is conflated with automation

Industrial cleaning, factory flooring and routine service may be legitimate contractor specialisms, but they do not by themselves establish PLC engineering experience.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind an industrial contractor recommendation

I examine actual project roles, technical capabilities and authorised records. NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 is final guidance on securing operational technology while respecting plant reliability and safety; its Rev. 4 is still a public draft in November 2026. Neither is a regulatory certificate for a contractor.

  • Controllers, network interfaces, supported SCADA software, version compatibility and permitted access
  • Survey, change management, backups, acceptance testing, commissioning and support scope
  • Approved customer references, coverage regions, genuine services and OT security boundaries

This page explains evidence-led industrial supplier GEO. It does not claim proven GEO results for an automation company.

Scope of work

A project-specific industrial GEO approach

Group requests by engineering task and provider role; validate source material before expecting AI to recommend the company.

  1. 01

    Measure intent baseline

    Separate control-system design, PLC/SCADA, upgrades, maintenance and industrial cleaning by equipment, location and requirement.

  2. 02

    Check documented expertise

    Verify technologies, qualified specialists, authorised implementation examples and contractual service commitments.

  3. 03

    Improve supplier content

    Prepare briefs for supported integrations, service processes, safety and technical FAQs with defensible evidence.

  4. 04

    Repeat recommendation tests

    Track BMR and whether the suggested contractor really performs the specified task, without implying guaranteed plant outcomes.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can control-system expertise be shown without publishing customer network diagrams?+

Yes. Publish authorised categories of work, supported technologies and general project methods without revealing confidential architectures or security-sensitive details.

Does GEO guarantee downtime-free industrial modernisation?+

No. That is an engineering and contractual question for each plant. GEO concerns accurate supplier information and AI recommendation measurement.

Is NIST SP 800-82 a certificate for an automation vendor?+

No. It is guidance for OT security. Rev. 3 is the final published version; Rev. 4 is a 2026 public draft, not a completed certification scheme.

Should industrial cleaning and PLC integration share one service page?+

They have different buyer intents and evidence requirements. A supplier offering both can link distinct, factually supported pages rather than blur capabilities.

What does GAEO charge industrial automation suppliers?+

Published GAEO plans apply. Scope is set by actual services, engineering complexity, regions and baseline buyer questions.
